hints: Describe power as a rate, making clear what quantity is transferred or done in each unit of time.
Use W for work done and place the time interval t in the denominator.
walkthrough: The controlled definition is: power is work done or energy transferred per unit time.
A per-unit-time rate is found by dividing by the time interval.
Using P for power, W for work done and t for time gives P = W/t.

ai_rubric.observable: States that power is work done or energy transferred per unit time
Writes P = W/t with the symbols identified consistently

hints: Choose the option that begins with work as force multiplied by displacement, not time.
After dividing work by time, the ratio s/t must become velocity.
walkthrough: For a constant force parallel to the displacement, W = Fs.
Power is work done per unit time, so P = W/t.
Substitution gives P = Fs/t = F(s/t).
Since s/t = v, the result is P = Fv, so option B is correct.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects B: W = Fs and P = W/t give P = F(s/t) = Fv

hints: Compare the direction of each candidate force quantity with the puck's eastward displacement.
A force component at right angles to motion does no work during that displacement.
walkthrough: The puck's velocity and displacement are eastward.
Mechanical power counts the rate of work done, so only a force component in the displacement direction contributes.
A perpendicular component has no displacement along its own direction and contributes zero power.
Therefore option B is correct.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects B: only the force component parallel to the eastward velocity enters P = Fv

hints: Convert the locomotive power from kilowatts to watts before rearranging the mechanical-power formula.
With P and v known, isolate force as F = P/v.
walkthrough: Convert 72 kW to 72000 W.
Rearrange P = Fv to F = P/v.
The correct selection is C.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects C: F = 72000/24 = 3000 N

hints: The cart's velocity is constant, so the resultant horizontal force is zero.
Match the motor's forward force to the stated 180 N resistance.
walkthrough: Constant velocity means zero acceleration and therefore zero resultant horizontal force.
The motor's driving force must balance the 180 N resistive force.
The driving-force magnitude is 180 N.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses constant speed to state that the 180 N driving force balances the 180 N resistive force

hints: Carry forward the 180 N driving force found from the constant-speed condition.
Multiply that force by the original 8.0 m s^-1 speed.
walkthrough: The relevant force is the 180 N driving force parallel to the cart's motion.
Use P = Fv.
The unit check is N m s^-1 = J s^-1 = W.

ai_rubric.observable: Substitutes the balanced driving force and speed into P = Fv
Obtains 1440 W or 1.44 kW with a suitable power unit

hints: The force remains 180 N, so substitute only the new 12 m s^-1 speed.
Explain the increase using energy transferred through more distance in each second.
walkthrough: Use the unchanged force in P = Fv.
At fixed force, P is directly proportional to v.
The cart moves through a greater distance each second, so the force does more work in each second.

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates the new power as 2160 W or 2.16 kW
Explains that at unchanged force a greater speed gives a greater energy transfer per unit time

hints: The 25 degree angle is measured from the horizontal velocity direction.
Use the adjacent component of the 2.4 kN tension and convert kilonewtons to newtons.
walkthrough: The sled velocity is horizontal, so resolve tension horizontally.
Convert 2.4 kN to 2400 N.
F_parallel = 2400 cos 25 degrees = 2175 N.
To two significant figures, the parallel component is 2.2 x 10^3 N.

ai_rubric.observable: Resolves the 2.4 kN tension parallel to motion using 2400 cos 25 degrees
Obtains a parallel component of approximately 2.18 x 10^3 N

hints: Carry the 2175 N horizontal tension component from part (a), including its unit.
Multiply that parallel component by the 3.5 m s^-1 sled speed.
walkthrough: Use the force component parallel to velocity, not the full cable tension.
P = F_parallel v = (2175)(3.5).
To two significant figures, the cable transfers 7.6 kW to the sled.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses P = F_parallel v with the resolved tension component and 3.5 m s^-1
Obtains approximately 7.6 x 10^3 W with a suitable unit

hints: Compare the vertical force-component direction with the sled's horizontal displacement.
Use the work-done condition before stating the power consequence.
walkthrough: The vertical tension component points upward while the sled velocity and displacement are horizontal.
The two directions are perpendicular.
There is no displacement in the vertical force component's direction, so that component does no work on this horizontal motion.
Zero work per unit time means zero contribution to the mechanical power.

ai_rubric.observable: States that the vertical tension component is perpendicular to the sled's horizontal velocity
Explains that no displacement occurs in the vertical component's direction, so it does no work and contributes zero power

hints: The platform speed is constant for the complete 48 s interval.
Multiply 2.5 m s^-1 by 48 s, keeping metres as the resulting unit.
walkthrough: Use s = vt for constant velocity.
The seconds cancel, giving s = 120 m.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses s = vt with 2.5 m s^-1 and 48 s
Obtains a distance of 120 m

hints: Carry forward the 120 m displacement from part (a).
The 620 N force and displacement are in the same horizontal direction, so no component resolution is needed.
walkthrough: For force and displacement in the same direction, W = Fs.

ai_rubric.observable: Substitutes 620 N and 120 m into W = Fs
Obtains 74400 J or 74.4 kJ

hints: Use the 74400 J work done from part (b) over the stated 48 s interval.
A rate of work is found by dividing work by time.
walkthrough: Power is work done per unit time.

ai_rubric.observable: Divides the 74400 J work done by the 48 s interval
Obtains 1550 W or 1.55 kW

hints: For the independent route, do not reuse the work or time values.
Multiply the original horizontal force directly by the constant speed, then compare numerical results.
walkthrough: Use P = Fv independently of the earlier work calculation.
This equals the 1550 W obtained from W/t.
The agreement is expected because P = Fv follows from W = Fs and P = W/t when s/t = v.

ai_rubric.observable: Independently calculates P = 620 x 2.5 = 1550 W using P = Fv
States that the Fv result agrees with the W/t result because P = Fv was derived from those same work and rate relationships

hints: The platform velocity remains horizontal, but the 620 N force is now angled.
Resolve the force horizontally with cos 40 degrees before multiplying by 2.5 m s^-1.
walkthrough: Only the force component parallel to horizontal velocity transfers energy into this motion.
F_parallel = 620 cos 40 degrees = 474.9 N.
To three significant figures, the new power is 1.19 x 10^3 W.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses the horizontal force component 620 cos 40 degrees in P = F_parallel v
Obtains approximately 1.19 x 10^3 W with a suitable unit
